content.value_statement: PowerShell projects need consistent structure, safe parameters, and current module guidance. This skill helps create scripts, modules, and GUIs using practical PowerShell references.
actual_capabilities: Drafts PowerShell script and function templates with CmdletBinding, validation, pipeline input, and ShouldProcess patterns.
Guides Windows Forms and WPF GUI creation with controls, layout patterns, and event handling examples.
Explains PSResourceGet and PowerShellGet commands for finding, installing, updating, and publishing modules.
Provides a bundled Search-Gallery.ps1 helper for PowerShell Gallery searches when live web tools are unavailable.
Encourages live verification of module availability, versions, and cmdlet syntax when current accuracy matters.
limitations: It does not execute PowerShell unless the user or agent explicitly runs a command.
Windows Forms and WPF guidance applies to Windows environments only.
Module versions and cmdlet syntax can change, so current details require live verification.
Generated scripts still need testing in the target PowerShell version and permission context.

use_cases.title: Create Production Scripts
use_cases.description: Build scripts with clear parameters, pipeline support, error handling, and comment-based help.

use_cases.title: Manage Gallery Modules
use_cases.description: Find, install, update, and publish PowerShell modules with PSResourceGet and PowerShellGet references.

use_cases.title: Build Desktop Utilities
use_cases.description: Create Windows Forms or WPF interfaces for internal tools and administrative workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PowerShell function for [task]. Include CmdletBinding, typed parameters, validation, and comment-based help.

prompt_templates.title: Add Pipeline Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this PowerShell function to support pipeline input, structured errors, verbose output, and safe ShouldProcess behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design a GUI Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PowerShell GUI for [workflow]. Include controls, event handling, layout guidance, and validation behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Module Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PowerShell module release plan for [module]. Cover manifest fields, dependencies, tests, Gallery publishing, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: I need a script that accepts server names and reports status.
output_examples.output: The response outlines a validated advanced function with pipeline input, clear errors, verbose logging, and safe output objects.

output_examples.input: Help me build a small Windows tool for selecting files and running a task.
output_examples.output: The response describes a Windows Forms layout, expected controls, event flow, validation rules, and user confirmation behavior.

output_examples.input: Recommend a module workflow for publishing my internal utility.
output_examples.output: The response explains manifest preparation, local validation, dependency checks, Gallery publishing choices, and version verification.

best_practices: State the target PowerShell version, operating system, and permission level before requesting generated scripts.
Use WhatIf, Confirm, validation attributes, and explicit parameter names for commands that can change state.
Verify Gallery modules and exact cmdlet syntax with live documentation when current accuracy is important.
anti_patterns: Do not install, update, or publish modules from generated guidance without explicit user approval.
Do not hardcode secrets, API keys, tokens, or local private paths in generated PowerShell.
Do not rely on aliases, positional parameters, or untested examples in production scripts.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create PowerShell GUIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes references for Windows Forms, WPF, controls, layout patterns, and events.

faq.question: Does it verify current module information?
faq.answer: It instructs live verification through documentation and PowerShell Gallery checks when accuracy is critical.

faq.question: Does it run PowerShell commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. Commands and the bundled gallery search script require explicit execution by the user or agent.

faq.question: Can it help publish PowerShell modules?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers manifests, PSResourceGet publishing commands, dry runs, and Gallery-related references.

faq.question: Is the GUI guidance cross-platform?
faq.answer: No. Windows Forms and WPF guidance is intended for Windows environments.
